author: Temminck, 1840
habitat: 습지와 소택지의 풀밭, 버드나무와 관목, 물가의 갈대밭
summary: 봄과 가을에 작은 무리를 지어 우리나라 전역을 지나가는 나그네새로, 습지나 소택지의 풀, 버드나무와 관목 덤불, 물가 갈대밭 등지에서 지낸다. 몸을 숨긴 채 좀처럼 모습을 드러내지 않으며 주로 곤충을 먹는다. 둥지는 풀 밑이나 땅에서 30cm 높이의 덤불 속에 짓는데 둘레가 흔히 풀로 가려져 있고, 6월 중순~7월 하순에 한배에 3~5개의 알을 낳는다. 한국을 비롯해 시베리아 동부, 캄차카, 만주, 사할린, 홋카이도, 혼슈 등지에서 번식하고 인도, 미얀마, 수마트라, 보르네오, 자바 등지에서 겨울을 난다.

art.subject: Lanceolated Warbler (Locustella lanceolata), adult on spring or autumn passage (sexes alike): upperparts olive-tinged brown, every feather of the crown, mantle and back with a broad blackish-brown centre, giving bold dense streaking; narrow, indistinct buffy-white supercilium; lores mottled buffy-white and dark brown; ear-coverts mixed olive-brown and buff; wings brown, the tertials dark-centred with pale edges; chin, throat and breast yellowish-white, finely marked with small triangular blackish-brown spots that form neat streaks continuing along the buff flanks; belly yellowish-white; undertail coverts buff with dark streaks; thin dark bill with a pale pinkish base below; dark eye; pinkish legs.
art.pose: creeping low in dense grass, partly hidden, side view
art.scene: Korean waterside reedbed and wet grassy marsh with willows and shrubs during spring or autumn migration; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view creeping low in grass: densely black-streaked olive-brown upperparts, faint buffy-white supercilium, small dark spots on throat and breast forming fine streaks along the flanks, yellowish-white belly, rounded tail, pink legs
adult, front view: yellowish-white throat and breast covered in small triangular blackish-brown spots arranged in neat lines, yellowish-white belly
art.build: Very small, skulking grasshopper warbler, about 11cm — smaller and slimmer than a sparrow, with a flat forehead and a slender, pointed bill shorter than the head. Legs pinkish and rather strong. Wings short; at rest the wingtips fall well short of the tail tip. Tail fairly short, broad and rounded. Moves mouse-like on or near the ground in dense grass, creeping and running rather than flying, the body held low and horizontal.
avoid: Do not leave the breast plain; neat dark streaks on the throat, breast and flanks are its key mark.
Do not paint the larger size, rufous rump and white-tipped dark tail of Pallas's Grasshopper Warbler (Locustella certhiola).
Do not paint a bold supercilium or a dark eye-stripe; the face is plain.
Do not paint bright yellow underparts; they are only faintly yellowish.
